fact: A 2018 practitioner Q&A states Senegal adopted the Cybercrime Law (Law 2008-10 of 25 January 2008), completing the Penal Code and Penal Procedure Code, and lists the offences and penalties of six months to 10 years; it says no separate cybersecurity act was yet adopted.
Infos du Jour reports the national police said on 16 April 2025 that it recorded 3,902 cybercrime complaints in 2024, cleared 223 and referred 194 people to prosecutors.
Le Soleil says Senegal's cybercrime law was promulgated on 25 January 2008 and governs the police Division speciale de cybersecurite.

Le Soleil reports Moustapha Diakhate was tried and sentenced on 28 November 2024 to two months in prison after a hearing at the Division speciale de cybersecurite for an insult committed through a computer system.
Le Soleil, citing the police 2024 annual report, says 3,902 of 18,951 offences were cybercrime complaints, of which 223 were cleared.
